items.question: Why are Life Span Development and Life Course Perspective treated as the main frameworks here?
items.notes: Likely when the student lists theories without recognizing which frameworks the professor treats as central.

items.question: What is the difference between Life Span Development and Life Course Perspective?
items.notes: Likely when the student says the theories sound similar but cannot explain the analytic difference.

items.question: Why is stage theory not enough for understanding aging here?
items.notes: Likely when a student leans too heavily on universal stage-based explanation.

items.question: How does historical context change the life course in this reading?
items.notes: Likely when the student mentions life course perspective but does not explain the role of historical context.

items.question: What counts as a turning point in the life-course perspective?
items.notes: Likely when the term is named but not defined through the reading.

items.question: What does linked lives mean, and why does it matter for aging?
items.notes: Likely when the student names the principle without explaining relational interdependence.

items.question: What does human agency mean in the life-course perspective?
items.notes: Likely when the student reduces people to passive products of structure.

items.question: Why is Glen Elder important in this reading?
items.notes: Likely when the student mentions the name but cannot explain the contribution.

items.question: What does Children of the Great Depression show about aging and life course?
items.notes: Likely when the example is recalled only as a title and not as an analytic case.
